provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The output colours the whole grid by stepping through a fixed 9-colour cycle (5,2,8,9,6,1,3,4,0). The step count is the Manhattan distance from the single seed cell, and the cycle starts at the seed's colour. Manhattan distance is unchanged by every D4 rotation or reflection. So the emitted program simply finds the seed in the visible coordinates and computes |dy|+|dx| directly; no axis or direction needs changing. Colour roles are fixed as constants: the background is palette[7] and the cycle is [palette[c] for c in the original cycle]. The seed is the cell that differs from the background. Every cell, the seed included, gets CYCLE[(index(seed)+distance) mod 9], so the seed keeps its own colour. The program works for rectangular grids of any size and for seeds on the boundary.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes exactly one non-background seed, as the constructor guarantees. If there are several, the first in row-major order is used. If palette[7] is missing from the grid, the background falls back to the most common colour. If the seed colour is not in the mapped cycle, which is impossible under the constructor, the input is returned unchanged. I found no fixture contradictions or constructor defects. The constructor's 8x8 size is preserved under D4.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Each input is an 8x8 grid of background 7 with one seed cell. Every output cell gets cycle[(idx(seed) + |dy| + |dx|) mod 9], using the fixed cycle 5,2,8,9,6,1,3,4,0, so each cell's colour depends on its Manhattan distance from the seed. The constructor stores the same cyclic order rotated as colors=[0,5,2,8,9,6,1,3,4] and indexes it by `index`. Because the factory looks the seed up with CYCLE.index(seed), the starting offset makes no difference.
evidence: Constructor: `grid[row][col] = colors[index]` and `output[r][c] = colors[(index + abs(r-row) + abs(c-col)) % 9]`. The only latents are the seed colour and the seed position, and both are visible in the input. No hidden random latent affects the labels.

The seed colour comes from a list that excludes 7, so the seed always differs from the background. There is always exactly one seed, leaving 63 background cells, so the BG constant and the `np.any(g == bg)` fallback are never reached ambiguously.

validate() reproduces the fixtures. index=7 gives colour 3 at (0,6). index=1 gives colour 5 at (5,2). index=0 gives colour 0 at (2,1). Spot check: pair-1 cell (7,0) has (7+13)%9=2, giving colors[2]=2, which matches the fixture.

Factory: CYCLE = [pal[c] for c in the rule cycle] and BG = pal[7]. These are consistent colour-role substitutions under the palette. Each cell is computed as CYCLE[(base+d)%n], with d=0 at the seed, so the seed keeps its colour. This is equivalent to the archived program, which copies the seed and fills rings d>=1.

D4 handling: Manhattan distance is invariant under every rotation and reflection. The solver finds the seed in visible coordinates and computes distances directly. There is no untransform/retransform wrapper.

Shared episode information: in an 8x8 grid, max(sy,7-sy) >= 4 and max(sx,7-sx) >= 4, so the maximum distance is always >= 8. Every demonstration output therefore contains distances 0 through 8 and shows all nine cycle colours in order. The fixed cycle is fully taught by any single demonstration, so the hard-coded CYCLE is not an undemonstrated arbitrary association.
The host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks and 16 fixture variants, with no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The solver assumes a single seed and takes the first non-background cell in row-major order. The constructor guarantees exactly one seed.
Returning the input unchanged when the seed colour is not in CYCLE is an out-of-domain fallback. The constructor excludes this case because the seed is always one of the nine cycle colours.
The cycle is hard-coded rather than read from the demonstrations. This is justified because every demonstration output reveals the complete cycle.
Only 64 positions times 9 colours (576) base inputs exist. The audit saw 474 unique base inputs, so diversity is limited by the task itself rather than by any defect.
required_context_checks: Confirm that the host palette permutation maps original colour 7 to the visible background and keeps the nine cycle colours distinct. The factory's BG=pal[7] and CYCLE mapping assume a bijective palette.

draft_notes.host_review: Reviewed rule and domain limitations. Host augmentation maps completed grids with one bijective palette, horizontal reflection then clockwise quarter turns; odd indices swap axes. Fresh audit iterates all eight variants, supplied fixture checks include query answers, and export requires every pair exact. Sampler exceptions are recorded rejections, not admitted examples. Spatial connectivity follows the stated constructor/archived mechanism; optional out-of-domain modes are not certified.
